objective: Classify all fractional extremizers for n>=5 via a signed-dual slack identity and prove the sharp one-unit gap, without transferring it to integer cp.

atomic_claims.text: The signed dual has the exact identity W=g_n(r)-(t-r+1)P-R-D, and all negative forward weights are bounded by D.
When r>=2 and t-r+1>=2, any departure from J(r,t) forces g_n(r)-W>=1.
For n>=5, lambda>B(n)-1 forces an extremal complete split graph with the explicitly listed core size; otherwise lambda and cp_f are at most B(n)-1.
Deleting one crossing edge from the smaller-core complete-split extremizer realizes cp=cp_f=lambda=B(n)-1 for every n>=5.

assumptions: Finite simple chordal graphs and exact edge partitions; the fractional parameters remain distinct from integer cp.
C18 signed duality and arbitrary-clique-suffix PEO argument, together with C01 matching construction.
The one-unit lemma assumes r>=2 and t-r+1>=2; classification assumes n>=5.
Allowed axioms: finite-graph-basic, finite-combinatorics, real-arithmetic; imported theorem dependencies require joint audit.
risks: Natural-language candidate only; no mathematical execution or verifier receipt.
Fractional extremizer classification does not classify integer cp extremizers.
The low-core slack inequality cannot be applied to the dense branch, or converted into an edit-distance estimate without proof.
The general integer rounding excess remains unbounded by this draft; target and root remain open.
